title: Genomic Characterization of Metastatic Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer
summary:
The West Coast Dream Team cohort is one of the few public resources that sequences metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer tissue rather than primary tumor, which is what makes it valuable: the biology that drives lethal prostate cancer is not well represented in primary-tumor cohorts. All 101 cases carry whole genome sequencing with copy number and structural variant calls, and 99 carry RNA sequencing.
The clinical annotation is unusual in shape. Disease state is recorded with complete consistency - every case is AJCC stage IV, every case has progression or recurrence recorded as "yes", and every case's last known disease status is distant metastatic recurrence or progression. But vital status is "unknown" for all 101 cases, and no treatment field is populated. The cohort tells you precisely where these patients were in their disease course and nothing about what happened to them next.
one_liner: 101 metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancers with whole genome and RNA sequencing from metastatic biopsies - every case stage IV with documented progression, and no usable vital status.

useful_for.question: What distinguishes the genome of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer from primary prostate cancer?
useful_for.rationale: Whole genome sequencing on all 101 metastatic biopsies pairs naturally with TCGA-PRAD's 500 primary tumors in the same repository under the same harmonization. The contrast is the cohort's clearest use and does not depend on any outcome field.
useful_for.statistical_note: The two cohorts differ in sequencing strategy and processing era as well as in disease state, so treat platform as a confounder rather than assuming harmonization removed it.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Which transcriptional programs mark androgen receptor pathway independence and neuroendocrine transdifferentiation in treatment-resistant disease?
useful_for.rationale: RNA sequencing on 99 metastatic biopsies is the right substrate for AR-signaling and neuroendocrine scoring, and metastatic tissue is where these phenotypes actually occur.
useful_for.statistical_note: Biopsy site varies across the cohort and contributes substantially to expression variance; include site as a covariate or stratify.

useful_for.question: How do structural variants and genome rearrangement patterns differ between metastatic sites?
useful_for.rationale: Structural variant calls exist for all 101 cases from whole genome rather than exome data, which is what makes rearrangement analysis credible here.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

useful_for.question: Can expression or genomic features predict which metastatic biopsies come from patients with the most aggressive disease trajectory?
useful_for.rationale: This is the question most people want the cohort for, and it is the one the harmonized records cannot support. It is listed here to be explicit that it requires outcome data obtained separately.
useful_for.statistical_note: Not answerable from the GDC records alone. Vital status is "unknown" for every case; outcomes must come from the marker publication's supplement or a dbGaP phenotype file.

limitations.statement: Vital status is populated for all 101 cases and informative for none - every value is "unknown". No overall survival endpoint exists in the harmonized records, despite a follow-up time being derivable for 87 of 101 cases with a median of 95 months.
limitations.mitigation: Outcome data are analyzed in the PNAS marker paper. Obtain them from its supplementary material or through dbGaP before planning any survival work.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

limitations.statement: No treatment field is populated: treatment type, therapeutic agents, treatment outcome and line of therapy are all empty. These are castration-resistant patients, so every one has had prior androgen deprivation and most will have had further systemic therapy, but which therapy and in what order is not recorded here.
limitations.mitigation: Do not attribute molecular features to specific treatments using these records. The absence of treatment annotation in a treatment-defined cohort is the single most important thing to know before selecting it.

evidence.note: Written by a named reviewer after reading the source documentation and the measured field coverage. Not machine-generated.

limitations.statement: 101 cases limits subgroup analysis sharply. Any stratification by biopsy site, molecular subtype or genomic alteration leaves groups in the low tens.
limitations.mitigation: Pre-specify a small number of hypotheses; treat subgroup results as exploratory.

limitations.statement: 86 of 101 cases are recorded as white and 5 as Black or African American, in a disease with pronounced incidence and mortality disparities affecting Black men.
limitations.mitigation: Do not use this cohort to characterise metastatic prostate cancer biology in Black patients; five cases cannot support it.
